To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the short‐circuit current of the toad colon is due to active sodium transport from mucosa to serosa, and this transport is inhibited by saline‐adapted toads.
the sodium pump of the toad colon is inhibited in the absence of aldosterone.
the toad colon can be isolated and maintained in vitro for 3–4 h, and that the short‐circuit current of the colon can be expressed quantitively by the net sodium flux.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a study of the effect of saline environment on the toad colon, with particular emphasis on the effect of aldosterone and the role of sodium transport in the maintenance of the transepithelial potential difference.
the effects of a saline environment upon the colon of the toad.

a comparison of the sodium transport mechanisms of toad colons isolated from toads which have been maintained for several weeks in a saline environment with those of colons from toads which were injected with aldosterone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aldosterone‐injection increases the net transport of sodium across the colon, whereas saline adaptation decreases it.
saline adaptation is accompanied by an increased sodium absorption by the toad colonic mucosa.
the sodium transport by the colon of the toad in saline is not dependent on aldosterone but is sensitive to changes in the sodium concentration on both sides of the epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the net sodium transport in the colon of the toad was not altered significantly by the saline environment.
the sodium pump of the colon was stimulated by the aldosterone injection, whereas in the saline‐adapted toad it was inhibited by the high sodium content of the environment.
the sodium pump is not saturated in saline‐adapted toads and is inhibited in saline‐adaptation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aldosterone is required for sodium transport by the colon of toads adapted to saline water.
the sodium transport of colons isolated from aldosterone‐treated toads is not affected by saline adaptation.
sodium transport by the colon of the toad Bufo marinus is a function of sodium availability in the environment and is not dependent on the presence of aldosterone.
